category: Data Protection Policies, Processes, and Procedures (PR.PO-P)
subcategory_text: A baseline configuration of information technology is created and maintained incorporating security principles (e.g., concept of least functionality)
informative_references: NIST SP 800-128: Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information Systems
NIST SP 800-70 Rev. 4: National Checklist Program for IT Products
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: CM-2 (Baseline Configuration), CM-6 (Configuration Settings), CM-7 (Least Functionality)
NIST PF 1.0 Core (January 2020): PR.PO-P1 (verified in NIST-Privacy-Framework-V1.0-Core.xlsx row 74)
implementation_examples: Define and document a baseline configuration for each technology asset class that processes personal data
Apply the principle of least functionality by disabling non-essential services, ports, and features
Detect and remediate configuration drift against the documented baseline on a defined cadence
assessment_objectives: Determine whether a baseline configuration is documented for assets processing personal data
Determine whether least-functionality principles are enforced by the baseline
Determine whether configuration drift is detected and remediated on a defined cadence
Determine whether baseline changes follow a documented change-control process
related_controls: ID.AM-P1 (NIST PF 1.0 — data inventory; see also PR.PO-P1 semantic note below)
semantic_note: PR.PO-P1 in NIST PF 1.0 addresses BASELINE CONFIGURATION management, not data inventory. The label 'Data inventory maintained' used in the AEGIS pilot spec maps more accurately to ID.IM-P1 ('Systems/products/services that process data are inventoried') in NIST PF 1.0. This file follows the authoritative NIST PF 1.0 subcategory text; user-facing taxonomy label may need reconciliation in a later iteration.
